We have written a dependency-ordered [action plan](../action-plan.qmd) for the remaining
surrogate work. It distinguishes completed local validation from performance measurements,
reference choices and subsequent verification.

The local transport checks are complete: [15 gradient, JIT, fallback and discrete-balance checks pass across RAPTOR and ITER hybrid in each mode]{.claim}[C-146](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-146){.cid .st-tested}. The final-model matched
runtime comparison remains open because its compute run was cancelled before execution.
The next performance step is to resolve that cancellation, agree a fresh bounded submission
and compare the final surrogate with reference transport at matched settings. Newton
profiling stays separate from the linear-solver timing comparison.

In parallel, the owner can choose the reference solvers or datasets for radio-frequency
(RF) and pedestal responses. That decision must specify channels, outputs, units, criteria
and Tier A fallbacks. The existing guards, grouped dataset interfaces and baseline trainer
are ready for those references; no predictive RF or pedestal model is trained.

After reference selection, we label a small grouped baseline, inspect errors and physical
integrals, agree accuracy targets, train ensembles and integrate them into TORAX behind
guards. Gradient, balance, fallback and coupled cost checks then define completion.

M3 closes only when all its required surrogate tasks meet the accuracy, differentiable
execution and speed-up criteria. Verification follows: agreed properties and trajectory
tolerances, formal proofs, uncertainty calibration, reference comparisons and certification
review. Local sampled checks remain distinct from those certificates.

This documentation update selects no new physics closure and submits no compute job.
The build log now follows the same sequence as the internal plan.
